Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We liked the latency profile and the KV caching example; the product seems like a good fit for a clinical-notes summarization pilot. A couple quick packaging questions from procurement before we draft an official statement of work:

1) For a 3-month pilot (low concurrency, bursty morning windows), do you recommend Compact or Core? Our primary concern is keeping unit cost predictable while being able to increase session length to ~1,200 tokens for some multi-note prompts.
2) If we start on Compact and need to upgrade mid-pilot, what does the rollback look like (price/proration, data migration, cached models)?
3) Are there short-term discounted pilot rates for health orgs evaluating security and audit logs?

I attached a short note with our expected throughput and a tentative timeline (Hightide-Pilot-MAP-draft.pdf).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

— Oliver

Hi Oliver —

Appreciate the deck — that helps. Short answers up front, details below so your procurement folks have something concrete to review.

1) Recommendation: start on Compact with a scoped headroom buffer (Compact + 2x burst pool) for the 3-month pilot. Compact keeps unit cost lower and our runtime can sustain 1,200-token sessions; performance soft-falls to Core only when you need sustained high concurrency.
2) Upgrade path: instantaneous model/route switch with hourly proration. Rolling back is allowed within the committed pilot billing window; we reverse proration for unused hours and provide a one-time migration check for KV cache compatibility. No customer data migration required — model artifacts and cache live in your dedicated session namespace.
3) Pilot discount: we generally offer a 20% pilot discount for early-stage pilots under 6 months for qualifying health customers, plus an evidence-sharing clause for latency/observability benchmarks.

I'll loop in Ben and Karthik to provide the exact numbers and a mock invoice for both Compact and Core options. If this looks good, we can produce a short mutual action plan and a 30-day notice rollback clause for the SOW.

Would you like the breakdown as an editable spreadsheet?

Best,
Lauren

Lauren / Oliver —

Attached is a quick spreadsheet (tier-comparison-compact-vs-core.xlsx) with sample monthly consumption rows for the pilot. Highlights: compact unit cost ~30% less at low concurrency for equivalent QoS; compact includes automatic prefix caching which will cut token spend on repeated clinical templates by ~18% on our benchmark.

Upgrade/rollback mechanics (short):
- Upgrade: immediate route change; billing shifts to new SKU at the top of the next hour; KV cache compatibility is automatic for model-compatible quantizations.
- Rollback: allowed within the pilot term; we credit unused hours proportionally to the new invoice and provide a one-time free re-quantization check if you change model variants.
- Attachments/provisioning: we can pre-provision a burst pool for the pilot (2 GPUs) that lives in your Dedicated pilot namespace; if you never hit burst capacity, no charge for the reserved burst for the first 14 days (trial window).

A few clarifying notes from procurement: we need a firm statement in the SOW about the 30-day rollback notice and how proration is calculated (UTC hour alignment? do you net usage across SKUs?). Also, any chance to extend the pilot discount to 25% if we commit to a 12-month renewal option at pilot completion (non-binding intent)?

Oliver

Oliver —

Agree on next steps. Answers:
- Proration: we bill on hourly blocks aligned to UTC. When you upgrade mid-hour, usage is pro-rated by the number of full token-hours consumed on each SKU in that UTC hour; credits applied to the next invoice. We'll include a proration example table in the SOW.
- Cache transfer: automatic for identical model families/quantization. If you switch model families or change tokenizer pre-processing, there may be a short re-index job (typically 10–45 minutes) to rebuild prefixes; we’ll schedule re-indexing during a low-traffic window you approve. We’ll also provide a one-time free warm-up run to seed the cache at pilot start.
- Discount: happy to offer 25% pilot discount if Hightide signs a non-binding 12-month renewal LOI within 30 days of pilot completion; we’ll capture that in the MAP as a conditional credit.

I'll draft the short MAP and a SOW appendix with the rollback clause + example proration math and share by EOD tomorrow. Ben / Mina — can you confirm the burst-pool reservation terms and include the reserve/no-charge 14-day trial line?

Thanks —
Lauren
